rows.exactSourceSentence: One kind gesture created a ripple in water across the team.
rows.sourceMeaning: An effect spreading from a small starting point; a water image.
rows.ownerMeaning: Spreading from a small beginning to affect others, through an explicit water-wave comparison.
rows.ownerGrammar: an action/feeling spreads like a ripple in water; like marks the comparison; specify what spreads and the observed response
rows.reason: The source uses created a ripple in water across the team, mixing a literal water noun with a figurative across-the-team result. Owner 1692 teaches an explicit like-simile. The effect is related, but this exact carrier is not a natural equivalent and a detector extension would launder awkward source wording.
rows.nextGate: Confirm a natural re-lemma such as ripple effect from the source before any alias; otherwise retain editorial hold.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A timetable is available at the tap of a screen.
rows.sourceMeaning: With a simple touch on a device; a fixed modern convenience phrase.
rows.ownerTitle: with a tap on the screen
rows.ownerMeaning: Obtain information or trigger an action through a simple touch on a device screen.
rows.ownerGrammar: with a tap on the screen; tap names a light touchscreen touch; say what is already open or available.
rows.ownerRegister: Literal digital-convenience pattern, not a nonliteral idiom. Natural learner form uses tap on the screen; exact source at the tap of a screen remains an alias.
rows.reason: The timetable-access meaning matches owner 829. The at the tap of a screen construction is attested but less usual than with a tap on the screen; a narrowly taught alternate can preserve the exact source without changing the digital-action outcome.
rows.nextGate: Review the at-the-tap grammar and add an exact bounded branch, source occurrence, and at least one assessed or takeaway contrast before aliasing; pair with repeat source 3140.

rows.exactSourceSentence: We should not paint it in black and white when both plans have merits.
rows.sourceMeaning: Present a complex matter as two simple opposites; a fixed colour metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaning: Clear-cut, with simple opposed categories and little ambiguity; often negated to acknowledge complexity.
rows.ownerGrammar: be/not be black and white; a black-and-white issue/decision uses hyphens before a noun. Both forms describe simple opposed categories in judgement, not monochrome images or in black and white meaning in writing.
rows.ownerRegister: Common idiom about distinctions or decisions.
rows.reason: The black-and-white binary judgement matches owner 309 semantically and its detector matches the embedded words, but paint it in black and white is an awkward/nonstandard carrier for this evaluative sense and can evoke literal painting. A regex substring alone is not enough.
rows.nextGate: Editor decides whether to preserve as a quoted source anomaly or normalize to see/portray it in black-and-white terms; no alias until carrier is reviewed.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The speech was all fireworks and not much substance.
rows.sourceMeaning: Exciting in appearance but shallow in content; fireworks is a figurative spectacle.
rows.ownerMeaning: Impressive presentation or publicity outweighs genuine practical value.
rows.ownerGrammar: More show than substance; compare visible display with what the event or proposal actually delivers.
rows.ownerRegister: Critical but natural commentary. A community organiser may use it when a launch event is lavish but promised services do not appear.
rows.reason: Fireworks versus substance expresses the owner 2961 show-versus-value judgement, but all fireworks and not much substance is a bespoke imagery variant absent from the owner target and assessment.
rows.nextGate: Resolve idiomaticity jointly with source 2966; only add a bounded imagery branch if naturalness and one assessed choice can be shown.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The school should keep that door wide open for beginners.
rows.sourceMeaning: Preserve access to an opportunity; a door metaphor.
rows.ownerTitle: open the door / the door is opening wider
rows.ownerMeaning: Create an opportunity for something to happen or develop; an opening door can describe access increasing.
rows.ownerGrammar: open a/the door to an opportunity; open the academic door metaphorically names access to formal study. Open, opens, opened and opening are normal forms.
rows.ownerRegister: Common figurative expression in conversation and writing.
rows.ownerTargetPattern: (?:\b(?:open|opens|opened|opening) (?:the|a) door(?:s)?\b|\bthe door (?:is|was) opening wider\b)|(?:\b(?:open|opens|opened|opening) the academic door\b)
rows.reason: Keep that door wide open preserves an existing route for beginners; owner 028 predominantly creates or widens an opportunity. Door-access imagery is shared, but maintenance versus opening is a distinct learner choice not yet covered.
rows.nextGate: Compare current 028 keys with maintenance sense; either explicitly broaden ownership and teach it or retain hold.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Community performances help keep their roots alive.
rows.sourceMeaning: Maintain a connection with cultural origins; a plant metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaning: Stay connected to origins or defining traditions while changing or growing.
rows.ownerGrammar: Keep + possessive + roots; roots is figurative. Explain both the origin retained and the new development.
rows.ownerRegister: Neutral reflective English. A community editor may use it when an old local magazine adopts a digital format.
rows.reason: Community performances sustaining cultural roots is the same origins-continuity decision as owner 4470. The existing detector already matches keep their roots inside the complete source; alive merely reinforces continued connection.
rows.nextGate: Attach exact source provenance and clarify alive as an optional modifier/continuity nuance without altering existing answer keys; consider a bounded full-expression control.

rows.exactSourceSentence: There is something electric about a small live concert.
rows.sourceMeaning: An exciting quality that feels energetic; electricity is figurative.
rows.ownerMeaning: The intense shared excitement or charged feeling of a particular event as it happens.
rows.ownerGrammar: feel/capture/miss the electricity of the moment; electricity is an excitement image, not a report about electrical supply. Identify whose impression and what moment.
rows.ownerRegister: Creative live-experience metaphor. Intensity does not guarantee artistic quality, attendance size or agreement among all people present.
rows.reason: Something electric about a concert reports a general energetic quality; owner 1062 names the intense shared excitement of a particular moment. Closely related image, but adjective construction and moment-specificity differ.
rows.nextGate: Review whether a broader electricity-family lesson would retain a single learner decision; otherwise keep held.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Investigators were working in the dark until the records arrived.
rows.sourceMeaning: Operating without information or guidance; a fixed light metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaning: Try to understand, answer or proceed without enough information, examples or guidance.
rows.ownerGrammar: Grope in the dark / groped / groping or guess in the dark / guessed / guessing; specify the information gap rather than imply the person lacks all ability. Guessing stresses an answer attempted without evidence.
rows.ownerRegister: Neutral figurative wording. A teacher may tell colleagues students are guessing in the dark when notes omit key examples; an organiser may grope in the dark when responses are scattered.
rows.ownerTargetPattern: \bgrop(?:e|es|ed|ing) in the dark\b|\bguess(?:es|ed|ing)? in the dark\b
rows.reason: Investigators working without records have the same information-gap decision as owner 1916 grope/guess in the dark. Working in the dark is natural agentive wording, but adds a different verb and can also be literal.
rows.nextGate: Add a bounded work-in-the-dark branch with figurative-context controls, source provenance and one keyed/takeaway teaching occurrence; independently check literal controls.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Trust is the invisible glue in a good team.
rows.sourceMeaning: A less visible quality that holds people together; a glue metaphor.
rows.ownerTitle: the glue that holds the group together
rows.ownerMeaning: The person or factor that keeps a group connected and functioning together.
rows.ownerGrammar: X is the glue that holds a group together; X can also act like glue, helping family or team members stay connected. The glue is metaphorical.
rows.ownerTargetPattern: (?:\bthe glue that holds the (?:group|team) together\b)|(?:\b(?:act|acts|acted|acting) like glue\b)
rows.reason: Trust as invisible glue keeping a team together is the same cohesion role as owner 110 the glue that holds a group together. The noun construction is different but does not create a new decision.
rows.nextGate: Add a bounded invisible-glue construction, exact source provenance, and assessed/takeaway coverage; test literal adhesive controls.

rows.exactSourceSentence: If the food is late, the mood can unravel.
rows.sourceMeaning: The atmosphere can lose coherence or break down; a fabric metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaning: Begin to break down or lose coherence, especially a plan, arrangement or relationship.
rows.ownerGrammar: a plan / arrangement / partnership starts to unravel
rows.reason: A mood unravelling suggests atmosphere deteriorating, but owner 1425 teaches a plan, arrangement or partnership beginning to lose coherence. The source omits start and the mood subject is less idiomatic.
rows.nextGate: Seek natural source usage for mood unravels and a defensible subject scope before changing 1425; otherwise hold.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The annual meal keeps family ties alive.
rows.sourceMeaning: Continuing connections among relatives; ties and life are figurative.
rows.ownerMeaning: Maintain affection or emotional closeness in personal relationships, including family ties.
rows.ownerGrammar: keep relationships/family ties warm, with or without their before relationships; keeping and kept mark ongoing or past care. Warm refers to emotional closeness.
rows.reason: Keeping family ties alive guarantees continuing connection; owner 1523 keep family ties warm specifically maintains affection or emotional closeness. An annual meal could do both, but the exact source does not establish warmth.
rows.nextGate: Retain hold unless owner brief and task can safely include existence/continuity as well as affection without conflating them.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The ceremony was all glitter and no substance.
rows.sourceMeaning: Attractive on the surface but lacking real value; a conventional contrast.
rows.ownerMeaning: Impressive presentation or publicity outweighs genuine practical value.
rows.ownerGrammar: More show than substance; compare visible display with what the event or proposal actually delivers.
rows.ownerRegister: Critical but natural commentary. A community organiser may use it when a launch event is lavish but promised services do not appear.
rows.reason: Glitter without substance shares owner 2961 surface-versus-value judgement and is more conventional than the fireworks variant, but its lexical imagery is not covered or assessed by that lesson.
rows.nextGate: Review idiomatic status and both 2349/2966 variants as one bounded family; avoid automatic alias based on semantic similarity alone.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Fair rules are the guardrails of social life.
rows.sourceMeaning: Rules that prevent harmful conduct while allowing freedom; a road metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaning: Create practical boundaries intended to reduce risk while leaving some room to act.
rows.ownerGrammar: put/putting up guardrails around an activity describes creating safeguards; people, rules or arrangements can also act as guardrails by limiting risk while leaving choices. Name what the boundary does and how people know it; it does not guarantee nothing can go wrong.
rows.ownerRegister: A parent explaining boundaries to another adult, or a coordinator discussing safeguards with volunteers, can use this neutral protective-barrier metaphor. The fairness of a particular limit still depends on the people and task.
rows.reason: Fair rules as guardrails limiting harmful conduct while allowing freedom matches owner 1965 protective boundaries. The source is a broad societal claim, whereas owner tasks use concrete rules; the metaphorical mechanism remains aligned.
rows.nextGate: Add a bounded are-the-guardrails-of-social-life/source variant and provenance, then assess a concrete rule example so the broad source claim does not overstate the lesson.

languageEvidence.limitations: Dictionary evidence supports general constructions, not automatic approval of every source carrier.
